_meta.name: dealer_territory_knowledge_base
_meta.description: Distributor regional management knowledge base v0 seed version — Knowledge items crystallized from this round of work (books/papers/real data/business dialogues), for the 04 allocation intelligence layer to retrieve when generating human recommendations.

schema.statement: Knowledge content (can be directly entered into the recommendation's reasoning chain)

items.statement: Regional exclusivity is a system arrangement that protects dealer investment, not a solution to an optimization problem. Dealers dare to invest (salespeople, vehicles, customer relationships) only if the investment will not be harvested by a neighboring dealer.
items.conditions: This is especially true under a buy‑out sales model.

items.statement: Carryover: last year's visit effort yields results this year. When evaluating territory changes, impact_horizon must be declared; otherwise, a short‑term sales dip after adjustment will be misread as adjustment failure.
items.conditions: Fast‑moving consumer goods (FMCG) categories driven by customer relationships.

items.statement: Adjustment disruption hurts mid‑size stores most: small stores rely on relationships, large stores rely on systems, mid‑size stores rely on both but are less stable.

Classic three‑step design method: (1) account‑level design (which stores belong to me) → (2) geographic consolidation (bundle adjacent stores) → (3) alignment adjustment (balance workload/potential). The fence is an output of step two, not a starting point.
Fence boundaries should follow main roads or rivers, recognizable by both sales teams, avoiding disputes. Cutting lines should always use visually obvious geographic features.
items.source: FENCE_CHARACTERISTICS_understanding.md (38 fence geometry verification: boundary long straight segments coincide with OSM main roads).

items.statement: Administrative boundaries are the base framework: outer suburbs are fully contracted (district/county purity ≈100%), older urban districts are split into 3–6 blocks.
items.conditions: Validated in Guangzhou market; other cities need re‑validation.
items.source: FENCE_CHARACTERISTICS_understanding.md (72% of fences have district/county purity ≥95%).

items.statement: Chain direct‑supply stores are not coverage gaps: supply to DIRECT_IN/DIRECT stores does not pass through the fenced dealer; it is a brand structural arrangement.
items.source: gz_data.json (Meiyijia chain 2,127 stores, 97% of direct‑supply stores).

items.statement: Upstream consistency of 85% is normal: within the fence, about 12% of stores have cross‑boundary supply (OOF) and 6% are direct supply; 100% consistency is unattainable and should not be pursued.
Identity first: before any allocation or diagnostic action, store identity must be resolved by rule 08. Gaps generated by stores with low identity_confidence may be false gaps.

Dealer change must assess relationship reliance: long‑term personal ties formed by reps are implicit glue for store renewal. Industry consensus transition: joint visit endorsement (old rep leads new 1–3 months) + three‑party chat group + VIP customer executive support. Reliance can be proxied by “same dealer continuous service years + visit stability” (sales metric to be confirmed).
items.source: This round of dialogue (Dashi case 40% reliance) + industry handover practice search 2026‑08‑28 (joint visit is consensus best practice).

items.statement: Low‑density market gaps are structural: industry practice is “wholesale/secondary distributor model (ultra‑low density) + central warehouse routed direct delivery (township) + separate visit‑sales delivery + online order supplement”, not adding staff. Service frequency by store tier (A: 1–2 visits/week, B‑C: bi‑weekly + online supplement).
items.conditions: Low store density and large travel radius
items.source: gz_conghua_gap analysis + industry low-density coverage practice search 2026-08-28
items.maps_to: Four-category diagnosis: resource shortage vs structural

items.statement: Contract is fill‑in text: authorized area is a textual description ('east of X road'), not a geometric polygon. Geometricizing the fence is essentially a manual interpretation of the contract.
Buy‑out sales + no‑reason no‑return: inventory and unsold risk borne by distributor. This is the economic root of territorial exclusivity.
Guangzhou status: 38 fences / 33,109 stores / OK 79% / OOF 12% / direct 6% / GAP 1% / MULTI 7 entities
Conghua whole‑area contract: fence nearly coincides with district boundary, single distributor covers whole area. Reflects 'suburban contracting' approach.
Panyu riverside cut: using the Chen Village waterway as boundary, each side belongs to different distributors, no dispute. Reflects 'natural boundary priority' approach.
items.source: This round of dialogue + map verification

items.statement: Dashi street adjustment assessment: when overall distributor is changed, 40% of stores have customer‑relationship dependency, requiring a transition plan (old rep visits 1‑2 months).
items.source: This round of dialogue (user business knowledge)

items.statement: Visit scheduling engine is read‑only (maintained by others): SRAF calls its public API via adapter, does not modify its code. Upstream upgrades need sentinel‑compatible detection.
Adjustment requires stability budget: number of stores/visits per round of changes is constrained by budget, confirmed visits are frozen. Large‑scale adjustments require approval chain.
items.source: visit phase3 design + SRAF 02 approval flow

items.statement: Regional health benchmark (Guangzhou v0): alignment ≥79% healthy; OOF rate >20% requires investigation; GAP needs four‑category diagnosis; MULTI must register conflict log.
items.conditions: v0 temporary benchmark, will be revised with ValidationPlan

items.statement: Graph partitioning (METIS/Spectral) + H3 hierarchical indexing is the modern solution: H3 lookup O(1) replaces point‑by‑point PIP; graph partitioning solves cross‑administrative alignment.

Sales rep capacity (China FMCG standard): normal 20‑30 stores/day; high‑density urban 30‑40; low‑density county/rural 15‑20. Store classification frequency: A class weekly 1‑2 visits, B class biweekly 1 visit, C class monthly 1 visit. Effective visit = order + standard actions (display/inventory/relationship), only check‑in without actions invalid.
items.maps_to: L3:Capacity; Diagnosis four categories: resource shortage benchmark

items.statement: International standard cross‑validation: General Trade 40‑45 visits/day, Strike Rate 60‑75% (MT 80%+), travel time <30‑40% of workday. Travel time overrun = poor route planning, not insufficient manpower.
items.conditions: In case of conflict with K‑BENCH‑003, use our company’s measured data (standard difference: effective visit definition differs).
items.maps_to: Diagnosis four categories: resource shortage benchmark

items.statement: Rebate structure determines dealer reaction to adjustments: tiered volume rebate → push/stockpiling impulse (pseudo growth); process rebate (display/exclusive‑sale/price credibility) → compliance execution. Industry practice: ~20% rebate tied to compliance. Predict dealer reaction by analyzing rebate structure first.

Dealer replacement standard SOP: approval chain Region Manager → Zone Director → Sales GM → Finance (account verification) → Legal (contract compliance); transition triple set: inventory clearance / payment settlement / customer handover list; transition period 1‑3 months joint visits. Strictly prohibit abrupt replacement.

Low‑density area service model selection: ultra‑low density → wholesale/secondary distribution (digitally equipped as delivery service provider); township level → central warehouse + route‑based direct delivery; combine physical visits with online ordering (cloud store/mini program), prioritize coverage depth over breadth, avoid large staffing.
items.maps_to: Diagnosis four categories: lack of willingness / structural; recommendation engine options

items.statement: Layer mirroring organization principle: decision level = organization level. Three‑level allocation independent (Layer‑D dealer region / Layer‑B rep route / Layer‑V visit schedule), upstream output = downstream given value, cross‑layer intervention prohibited; each layer independently evaluated and approved; overlap prevention + white‑zone prevention apply at each layer.
items.conditions: Distribution management system design general principles
items.source: Industry organization structure search 2026‑08‑28 + user decision “Each layer independent, do not interfere”
items.maps_to: World model §2A three levels; diagnosis first identifies level then attributes cause

items.statement: Route design five‑step method (Layer‑B): fix points (store inventory classification) → define area (geographic zoning) → assign rep (area to rep) → define frequency (per ABC) → define route (path ordering).

Route four principles: ① area‑based (geographic proximity to avoid backtracking, start dense then sparse) ② classification‑based frequency (ABC: A weekly / B biweekly / C monthly) ③ load balancing (Σ stores × frequency equal across routes) ④ fixed routes to cultivate relationships. Route = commitment to store visits (PJP), GPS verification of fulfillment.

Layer‑B/V process baseline: visit achievement redline 90% (below → performance deduction; above 95% → reward); supervisor co‑visit 50‑70% of work hours; sales rep evaluation weight reference: process 40% + result 40% + enablement 20%.

Decision object for territory adjustment is [region/zone] (territory); store attribution is a derived effect (F3 footprint follows F2 fence). Treating “store” as the decision object is a misalignment from the CRM data‑sync perspective—region is the primary actionable entity.
items.conditions: FMCG sell‑out model; stores within region automatically follow region assignment.
items.source: Business‑side correction 2026‑08‑28 (“Should not be phrased as store; if it were a store you could directly modify it in CRM; in reality it is a region, store is an added effect”).
items.maps_to: World model F2 fence = decision object / F3 store = derived effect; adjust.py region‑priority engine.

knowledge_gaps_needing_business_input: Customer‑relationship dependency quantification: industry has no standard metric; propose using “continuous service years with same dealer + visit stability” as proxy; business must confirm calculation method (impacts K‑CASE‑003 40% reproducibility).
Approval chain localization: K‑RULE‑009 is industry default five‑level; must verify against our company’s actual org structure.
